title: Affine Perverse Vanishing And Universal Hyperplanes

items.title: Affine algebraic Whitney strata admit distance exhaustions with finitely many stratified Morse points
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $Z\subset\mathbb C^N$ be closed algebraic and let $\mathcal S$ be a finite Whitney stratification by smooth locally closed complex algebraic strata. In every prescribed nonempty real open subset of the parameter space $\mathbb C^N$, there exists $a$ such that $\phi_a(z)=\|z-a\|^2$ is a proper strongly plurisubharmonic exhaustion of $Z$, its restriction to each stratum has only nondegenerate critical points, there are finitely many such points in total, and at every critical point $p\in S$ its ambient differential is nonzero on every limiting tangent space of another stratum approaching $p$. Multiple critical points may have equal critical values; the Statement makes no unsupported distinct-value assertion. The same conclusion applies on any closed affine complex algebraic embedding of $Z$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Source: Goresky-MacPherson, Stratified Morse Theory, Part I SS2.2.3-2.2.4 (existence of Morse functions: the parameter map Phi(a,x)=d(phi_a)(x) to the cotangent bundle is a submersion outside a null set) and SS2.3.1 (nondegenerate conormals form an open dense set). Step 1 (bad limiting covectors are null). On a Jacobian chart of a stratum S of complex dimension s the algebraic conormal bundle has complex dimension N, and its boundary inside the closure has complex dimension at most N-1; a covector at a point of the closure that kills a limiting tangent plane of S lies in that boundary. Step 2 (degenerate critical points are null). The real critical incidence I_S={(a,z): z in S, d(phi_a|S)_z=0} is the real normal bundle of the stratum, of real dimension 2N; its differential to the parameter space C^N is surjective exactly where the stratum Hessian is invertible, so Morse-Sard makes the degenerate parameters null, and a finite union of null sets is null. Step 3 (forbidden limiting tangents are null). Identify real ambient covectors with complex covectors by lambda -> Re lambda; the inverse image of each smoothing stratum of the conormal boundary has real dimension at most 2N-2, hence null projection to the parameter space. Step 4 (finiteness and the choice of a). Complexify the squared distance to F(z,w)=sum (z_k-u_k)(w_k-v_k) on S x conj(S); the complex critical incidence is the algebraic conormal bundle of S x conj(S), of complex dimension 2N, and the generic-fibre dimension supplier gives a nonempty complex Zariski open of parameters over which its fibres are zero-dimensional, hence finite. The real diagonal (u,v)=(a,bar a) is Zariski dense in the complex parameter space and every prescribed nonempty real open is Zariski dense in that diagonal, so a real parameter outside the finitely many null exceptional sets exists; real stratum critical points lie in the complex fibres because real diagonal tangent vectors (t,bar t) span the complex tangent space at (z,bar z). Step 5 (conclusion). For such a, phi_a is proper on the closed set Z, its ambient Levi form is positive definite, each stratum restriction has finitely many nondegenerate critical points, and no critical point kills a limiting tangent plane. Equal critical values are allowed; no stratified product theorem or complex-link theorem is used.

references.title: M. Goresky and R. MacPherson, Stratified Morse Theory, Ergebnisse der Mathematik 3. Folge Band 14, Springer 1988 (author-hosted complete book scan)
references.locator: Part I §2.2.3-2.2.4 (existence of Morse functions; density of good distance parameters) and §2.3.1 (nondegenerate conormals are open and dense)

items.title: Complex stratified Morse data, constructible transport and complex links
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $Z$ be a complex algebraic variety with a finite smooth complex algebraic Whitney stratification, and let $A$ be a bounded algebraically constructible complex of finite-rank sheaves over any field $k$, locally constant on these strata. At a nondegenerate stratified critical point $p$ of a smooth real function $f$, on a stratum $S$ of complex dimension $s$, require that its tangent Hessian is invertible and $df_p$ kills no limiting tangent plane of an incident upper stratum. Let $\lambda$ be its real tangent Morse index. There are sufficiently small adapted compact critical-band neighborhoods whose local relative cochain complex is the normal relative complex shifted by $-\lambda$. The normal relative complex is canonically the restriction cone

$$\operatorname{Cone}\bigl(A_p\longrightarrow R\Gamma(\mathcal L,A|_{\mathcal L})\bigr)[-1],$$

where $\mathcal L$ is a collared complex link obtained by intersecting a transverse complex affine normal plane with a nonzero nearby generic complex linear level and a small closed ball. An empty link has zero cochains. The identifications transport the actual relative restriction maps and hold for the stated constructible coefficients, not just constant coefficients.

For a proper strongly plurisubharmonic stratified Morse exhaustion with finitely many critical points, the relative cochains across each critical value are the finite direct sum of these local complexes. Regular bands, including the ray above the last critical value, preserve actual constructible cohomology. Such an affine exhaustion is supplied by the stated distance-exhaustion lemma. If $d$ is any upper complex dimension for $Z$, the complex link at an $s$-dimensional stratum has dimension at most $d-s-1$. Unrefined link strata have the original codimensions relative to these upper dimensions; further compatible refinement only weakens a stalk-degree bound expressed using codimension.

For these algebraic ball-cut links, one can refine globally on the closed affine complex section, choose a nearby radius and generic distance center preserving its collar, and identify closed-link cohomology with the open ball cut. On that open cut $-\log(R^2-\phi_a)$ is a proper strongly plurisubharmonic exhaustion with finitely many nondegenerate stratified critical points and the same indices as $\phi_a$. The link itself is not asserted to be a closed affine variety. All product identifications are conditional only on the named topology, incidence and sheaf suppliers; no decomposition theorem, arithmetic purity or affine paving is assumed.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Goresky-MacPherson, Stratified Morse Theory, Part I Ch. 4-8 (moving the wall, fringed sets, absence of characteristic covectors, well-definedness of local/normal/tangential Morse data, proof of the main theorem 8.1-8.5.10) and SS12.1-12.6 (normal Morse data of two functions; Milnor fibration of the normal slice), Part II Ch. 2-3 (complex link, its independence and the homotopy type of the Morse data); Goresky, Morse theory, stratifications and sheaves SS1.7.6 Lemma 2 (constructible cone-stalk comparison) and SS1.8.1-1.8.2 (sheaf Morse groups and the relative disk shift). Step 1 (normal form). Straighten the critical complex stratum by a holomorphic graph chart and apply the Morse lemma only to the real tangent coordinates; write g=-|x_-|^2+|x_+|^2, q=|x|^2, rho=|n|^2, r=q+rho, t=f-g. Whitney A gives bounded horizontal right inverses and Whitney B puts limiting unit normal secants in the limiting vertical tangent kernels. Step 2 (characteristic radial estimates). At normal radial characteristic points drho=B dt; normalizing by |n| and passing to a limiting vertical tangent kernel gives |t| comparable to |n| and sign B=sign t, and a bounded horizontal correction with dtH=0 gives 2|x|^2+o(|n||x|)=2(A+B)g at dr=A dg+B df; the complementary normal-dominant and tangent-dominant arguments give the required uniform independence of the radial mixed forms over coefficients in [0,1]. Step 3 (wall motions). The explicit transverse wall families of Construction A carry the relative lower-face union through the two normal-wall rotations and the moving-wall equality; the controlled stratified submersion supplier transports the relative lower face throughout, and the endpoint is the product of the normal band pair and the tangent quadratic pair. Step 4 (derived coefficient transport, not homotopy invariance). Triangulate the compact controlled source with the compact triangulation supplier, use acyclic constant-coefficient complexes on contractible cells times the parameter interval, and use the product projection adjunction unit of the finite incidence model to prove pullback fully faithful; closed-skeleton induction lifts connecting morphisms and finite cones, so endpoint cohomology, relative cones and restriction arrows are transported together for the stated constructible coefficients, over every field. Step 5 (complex link). On the complex affine normal plane put h=w-i w circ i, where w is the real normal differential; complex limiting tangent planes give rank two for its real components, interpolation from the normal function to Re h preserves the first jet and uniform normal nondegeneracy, and Whitney B on h=0 gives joint rank for rho and both components. The map h is a proper stratified submersion on the compact cut 0<|h|<epsilon to the punctured disk, so controlled transport trivializes it over the convex half-disk and the negative-side cochains are identified with RGamma(L,A|L) for the collared complex link L; cofinal nested cylinders have quasi-isomorphic restriction maps. Step 6 (normal Morse triangle). Two explicit normal wall rotations expand the normal band to the whole ball relative to its negative outer cap; the transported lower face is the persistent moving-wall equality cut at u<=-eta, and controlled radial contraction together with the regular collar identifies cap cochains with negative-side cochains and the whole-ball cochains with the stalk A_p. Ordinary localization gives the cone arrow A_p -> RGamma(L,A|L) and the shift [-1], including the empty-link case (zero cochains). Step 7 (tangential shift and global attachment). The negative tangent disk pair has relative cochains k in degree lambda and the positive tangent disk contributes degree zero, so tensoring with the normal complex proves the shift [-lambda]; relative excision after removing disjoint adapted critical neighborhoods, the acyclicity of side/bottom pairs of the regular height product, and the controlled transport give the finite direct sum over critical values, with equal critical values handled by a finite disjoint union. Regular bands and the ray above the last critical value preserve constructible cohomology. Step 8 (nonpure dimensions and the algebraic ball cut). For an allowed upper complex dimension d and a critical stratum of dimension s, transverse link strata have dimension at most d-s-1 and unrefined codimensions equal d-dim R; refinement only weakens a codimension-codified stalk bound. On the closed affine section refine globally, choose a regular radius in the original collar and a nearby generic distance center preserving it, and identify the closed ball-cut link with the open ball cut; on the open cut -log(R^2-phi_a) is a proper strongly plurisubharmonic exhaustion with the same finite critical points and Hessian indices, closing the ball-link clause without treating the link as affine. No decomposition theorem, arithmetic purity or affine paving is used.

items.title: Smooth and noncharacteristic complex pullbacks are perverse-exact
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $P$ be a bounded algebraically constructible complex on a complex variety $Y$ with a finite complex algebraic Whitney stratification. If $a:X\to Y$ is smooth of pure relative complex dimension $d$, then $a^*[d]$ is perverse-exact and $a^!=a^*[2d]$ in complex orientation. If $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ is the restriction of a smooth complex closed embedding of codimension $c$ transverse to every stratum, then $i^*[-c]$ is perverse-exact and $i^!P\cong i^*P[-2c]$. The latter comparison is for complexes constructible for that transverse stratification; no assertion is made for arbitrary closed embeddings.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited AC. Sources: de Cataldo-Migliorini SS3.5 (Lemma 3.5.4: a normally nonsingular inclusion of complex codimension c satisfies i^!K = i^*K[-2c]) and SS3.7 (t-exactness; smooth pullback with the relative-dimension shift is t-exact, with Remark 3.5.1), and BBD SS4.2.3-4.2.4 (a smooth map of relative dimension d satisfies f^! = f^*[2d](d) and f^*[d] is t-exact). Step 1 (smooth pullback, upper aisle). If A is in the upper middle-perverse aisle, a support of H^{q+d}(A) has dimension at most -(q+d); its inverse image under a smooth relative-d map has dimension at most -q, which is exactly the upper support condition for a^*A[d], since ordinary pullback of field-module sheaves is exact. Step 2 (smooth pullback, lower aisle). The ordinary six-operation construction gives Da^*=a^!D and the complex orientation gives a^!=a^*[2d]; hence D(a^*A[d])=a^*DA[d], so applying Step 1 to DA proves preservation of the lower aisle. Step 3 (transverse closed embedding, upper aisle). If i:Z->Y is the restriction of a smooth closed embedding of codimension c transverse to every stratum, a stratum S of dimension s meets Z either trivially or in dimension s-c, so the support of H^{q-c}(P) meets Z in dimension at most -(q-c)-c=-q, the upper perverse condition for i^*P[-c]. Step 4 (exceptional comparison). In the controlled normal product supplied by the local trivialization, a constructible complex is constant along the normal c-disk, so its exceptional restriction is i^*P tensored with the relative normal cochain complex of (D^{2c},S^{2c-1}); the oriented relative generator identifies this with k[-2c], and the local comparisons glue because complex-linear determinants have positive real determinant, so the same normal orientation generator is used on overlaps. Step 5. Dualizing Step 3 gives the lower-aisle exactness i^*[-c] is perverse-exact, proving both exactness assertions and both oriented exceptional-pullback formulas, including relative dimension and codimension zero. No affine vanishing, decomposition theorem or Hodge theory is an input.

references.locator: Lemma 3.5.4 (normally nonsingular inclusion: i^!K = i^*K[-2c]) and §3.7 with Remark 3.5.1 (t-exactness of smooth pullback)

items.title: Artin vanishing on complex affine varieties
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction. If $Z$ is a complex affine algebraic variety of complex dimension $d$ and $F$ is an algebraically constructible sheaf of finite-dimensional $k$-vector spaces, then $H^q(Z,F)=0$ for $q>d$. More precisely the bound is the dimension of the closure of its support. If $P\in{}^pD^{\le0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q>0$. If $P\in{}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Z;k)$, then $H_c^q(Z,P)=0$ for $q<0$. The empty variety and zero coefficients give zero groups.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction. Sources: Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves, Theorem 13.7 (local Morse data for constructible coefficients) and SS17 (Theorems 17.7 and 17.9), together with the local stratified Morse product and complex-link description supplied by [[lem-complex-stratified-morse-data-have-tangential-normal-product-and-link-description]]. Step 1 (tangential index bound). On a complex manifold of complex dimension s a strongly plurisubharmonic function has tangent Morse index at most s: otherwise the negative Hessian subspace would contain a real two-plane spanned by v and sqrt(-1)v, on which the Hessian sum would be a positive multiple of the Levi form, contradicting negativity. Step 2 (codimension induction). Suppose the stalks of a constructible complex A satisfy H^q(A)_x=0 for q>d-s on every stratum of complex dimension s, and set c=d-s. At a codimension-c stratum, the complex link has dimension at most c-1; use c-1 as the allowed upper dimension, even for nonpure links. An empty link has zero cohomology. A critical point of the collar-compatible logarithmic exhaustion on the link lies on a link stratum of dimension c-1-c' with c'<c, whose unrefined stalk bound holds by hypothesis and only weakens under refinement; by induction its normal Morse cohomology vanishes above c' and the Morse index is at most c-1-c'. The long exact sequences at the finitely many critical values then make the link cohomology vanish above c-1, and the collared-link and regular-interval clauses identify this with the full complex link. Step 3 (normal triangle). The stalk term of the normal Morse triangle vanishes above c by hypothesis and the link term in degree q-1 vanishes above c-1 by Step 2, so normal Morse cohomology vanishes above c; this completes the codimension induction. At the top dimension d, the normal degree is at most d-s and the tangential index at most s, so each relative group vanishes above d, and the finitely many critical-value sequences together with the regular interval above the last value give H^q(Z,A)=0 for q>d. Step 4 (sharpened support bound). A degree-zero constructible sheaf satisfies the stalk hypothesis, giving the dimension-d bound; replacing Z by the closed algebraic support closure of F and using extension by zero gives the sharpened bound q>dim(supp F). Step 5 (perverse consequences). For P in the upper perverse aisle the hypercohomology spectral sequence E_2^{a,b}=H^a(Z,H^b(P)) has H^b(P) supported in dimension at most -b, so E_2^{a,b}=0 whenever a+b>0, and boundedness gives H^q(Z,P)=0 for q>0. For P in the lower aisle apply this to DP and the finite constructible duality H_c^q(Z,P)=H^{-q}(Z,DP)^vee to obtain H_c^q(Z,P)=0 for q<0. The empty variety and zero coefficients give zero groups.

references.title: M. Goresky, Lecture Notes on Sheaves and Perverse Sheaves (version of June 26, 2026)
references.locator: §13 (Morse theory with constructible coefficients) and §17.7, §17.9 (complex-link vanishing and Stein/affine vanishing)

items.axiom_use: AC is assumed as inherited from the constructible derived-category construction, consumed through [[lem-complex-stratified-morse-data-have-tangential-normal-product-and-link-description]] and the AC-declared distance-exhaustion supplier [[lem-affine-algebraic-whitney-strata-admit-finite-critical-strongly-plurisubharmonic-distance-exhaustions]]; the perverse spectral sequence and duality steps are choice-free.

items.title: Affine morphisms have one-sided perverse exactness
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. For an affine morphism $u:X\to Y$ of complex algebraic varieties and finite-dimensional field coefficients, $Ru_*$ sends ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ and $Ru_!$ sends ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(X)$ into ${}^pD^{\ge0}_c(Y)$. More precisely a bounded constructible $K$ belongs to ${}^pD^{\le0}_c(Y)$ if and only if $H^q(V,K)=0$ for every affine Zariski open $V\subset Y$ and every $q>0$.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited AC. Source: BBD SS4.1.1-4.1.8 (Theorem 4.1.1: for an affine morphism Rf_* is left t-exact; Corollary 4.1.2 and the relative version of 4.1.7-4.1.8 characterize the upper perverse aisle by the vanishing of H^q(V,-) on affine opens V). Step 1 (local-system detector). Let U be a smooth irreducible affine variety of dimension i>=1 and L a nonzero finite-rank local system. Noether normalisation and the affine-dimension theorem give i functions whose common zero set S is finite and nonempty; local complex orientation and local constancy identify H_S^{2i}(U,L) with the nonzero sum of the stalks L_s, while absolute Artin vanishing gives H^{2i}(U,L)=0, so the support long exact sequence gives H^{2i-1}(U setminus S,L) nonzero. Cover U setminus S by the i principal opens D(f_j); every finite intersection is affine, so absolute Artin vanishing bounds its cohomology by i, and the Cech index is at most i-1; in total degree 2i-1 only H^i(D(f_1...f_i),L) can contribute, so it is nonzero. For i=0 the detector is the nonzero stalk at an isolated point. Step 2 (converse characterization). Suppose all positive-degree H^q(V,K) vanish for affine opens V of Y. Write U_i=Y setminus F_{i-1} and argue downwards in i that the stalk cohomology on U_i satisfies the upper perverse support bound. On U_i put A=tau_{<=-i}K and Q=tau_{>-i}K; the induction hypothesis and the layer bound make A upper perverse, so on each affine V the triangle A->K->Q gives H^q(V,Q)=0 for q>0, and all cohomology sheaves of Q are local systems supported on the closed smooth layer W_i. If Q is nonzero, let b>-i be its largest nonzero cohomological degree and L=H^b(Q)|_{W_i}; the detector supplies an affine V inside U_i with H^i(V cap W_i,L) nonzero, and the bounded spectral sequence H^a(V cap W_i,H^t(Q)) => H^{a+t}(V,Q) has a unique nonzero term in total degree i+b>0, a contradiction; hence Q=0 and the induction closes. Step 3 (application). For P in the upper perverse aisle on X and an affine open V subset of Y, the inverse image u^{-1}V is affine, so derived composition and absolute Artin vanishing give H^q(V,Ru_*P)=H^q(u^{-1}V,P)=0 for q>0; the characterization then puts Ru_*P in the upper aisle. For P in the lower aisle apply this to DP and dualize (D Ru_* D = Ru_!) to obtain the claim for Ru_!. Empty and zero cases follow from the same zero triangles. The arithmetic-purity step of BBD 4.1.7 is replaced by the explicit oriented complex local cohomology detector; no Stein local-characterization theorem or nonproper restriction claim is used.

references.title: A. A. Beilinson, J. Bernstein, P. Deligne, Faisceaux pervers, Asterisque 100 (1982)
references.locator: §4.1.1-4.1.8 (affine morphisms are t-exact on one side; the affine-open characterization of the upper perverse aisle)

items.title: General projective hyperplanes decrease the defect of semismallness
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective morphism of complex projective varieties with $X$ smooth, nonempty and irreducible of dimension $n$. Fix a projective embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ with $d\ge1$ and let $Y_i=\{y:\dim f^{-1}(y)=i\}$. Put $r(f)=\max_{Y_i\ne\varnothing}(2i+\dim Y_i-n)$. For the universal hyperplane incidence $g:\mathcal X\to Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$ one has $r(g)\le r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$. If $r(f)=0$, $g$ is small: it has defect zero and every positive-fiber-dimensional stratum gives a strictly negative defect contribution.

There is a nonempty Zariski open subset of the hyperplane parameter space such that every hyperplane $H$ in it has smooth $X_H=X\cap H$ and satisfies the same conclusions for $f_H:X_H\to Y$: its defect is at most $r(f)-1$ if $r(f)>0$, and it is small if $r(f)=0$. Empty hyperplane sections are omitted from the defect computation and have zero pushforward. Successive general sections therefore lower a positive defect at every nonempty step. A finite prescribed algebraic Whitney stratification can also be met transversally by shrinking this open subset when the separately supplied stratified transversality theorem is applicable.
items.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers. Source: de Cataldo-Migliorini, Theorem 4.7.4 (r(f) goes down) and its proof. Step 1 (universal incidence). The incidence X={(x,H): x in X cap H} is the total space of a projective-space bundle of relative dimension d-1 over X, because the linear forms vanishing at a point form a rank-d subbundle of the dual of the ambient linear space; hence X is smooth of dimension n+d-1. The fibre of g at (y,H) is f^{-1}(y) cap H, and a nonempty hyperplane cut of a projective variety of dimension i+1 is pure of dimension i unless the hyperplane contains a top-dimensional component, in which case it is i+1. Step 2 (universal bound). Partition the universal locus of fibre dimension i into A_i, where dim(f^{-1}(y) cap H)=i with y in Y_i, and B_i, where y in Y_{i+1}; both are constructible by upper semicontinuity of projective fibre dimension. For fixed y in Y_i, hyperplanes containing a top-dimensional component of f^{-1}(y) form a parameter locus of dimension at most d-i-1, so componentwise generic-fibre dimension bounds give dim A_i <= dim Y_i + d-i-1 and dim B_i <= dim Y_{i+1}+d; subtracting n+d-1 from twice the fibre dimension plus these parameter dimensions gives contributions at most r(f)-i and at most r(f)-1, while the A_0 bound is dim Y_0-n <= 0. Hence r(g) <= r(f)-1 when r(f)>0; if r(f)=0 the bounds are strictly negative for i>0 and zero is attained on the dense image of the generically finite map, so g is small. Step 3 (fixed general hyperplane). Project each of the finitely many locally closed components of A_i and B_i to the dual projective space; components with nondense image are absent from a general parameter fibre, and components with dense image have general parameter-fibre dimension at most their dimension minus d. Intersecting the resulting nonempty parameter opens with the Bertini smooth-section open and repeating the arithmetic of Step 2 with source dimension n-1 and parameter dimension d gives the fixed-hyperplane conclusions, including smallness when r(f)=0; empty hyperplane sections are omitted and have zero pushforward. Iterating on the successive smooth nonempty sections lowers a positive defect at every step. The prescribed finite stratified transversality clause is the separately supplied condition named in the Statement, not a consequence of ordinary Bertini alone. No counting-of-constants theorem asserting that a hyperplane avoids every fibre component is needed.

references.title: M. A. A. de Cataldo and L. Migliorini, The Hodge theory of algebraic maps, arXiv:math/0306030v2 (complete final-version PDF)
references.locator: Theorem 4.7.4 and its proof (defect r(f), universal hyperplane family)

items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the algebraic dimension and Bertini suppliers [[thm-upper-semicontinuity-fibre-dimension-projective]] and [[thm-bertini-smooth-hyperplane-section]] and from the published dimension suppliers [[cor-dimension-of-image-plus-generic-fibre]] and [[lem-projective-hypersurface-dimension-drop]]; the incidence, componentwise generic-fibre and parameter-fibre estimates are otherwise choice-free.

items.title: Universal hyperplanes give relative weak Lefschetz and maximal pullback subobjects
items.statement: Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a projective map of complex varieties, with a fixed closed embedding $X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^d$ and $d\ge1$. Set $Y'=Y\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p:Y'\to Y$, $X'=X\times(\mathbb P^d)^\vee$, $p':X'\to X$, and let $i:\mathcal X\hookrightarrow X'$ be the universal hyperplane incidence. Write $g=(f\times1)i$, and for $K\in\operatorname{Perv}(X;k)$ put $M=i^*p'^*K[d-1]$. Then $M$ is perverse and the restriction/Gysin maps give isomorphisms $p^*{}^pH^l(Rf_*K)[d]\to{}^pH^{l+1}(Rg_*M)$ for $l\le-2$ and monomorphisms for $l=-1$, with dual isomorphisms for $l\ge2$ and epimorphisms for $l=1$. In particular $p^*{}^pH^{-1}(Rf_*K)[d]$ identifies with the largest perverse subobject of ${}^pH^0(Rg_*M)$ belonging to the essential image of $p^*[d]$, and $p^*{}^pH^1(Rf_*K)[d]$ with the largest such quotient.
items.strategy: Assume the inherited AC. Sources: BBD SS4.2.5-4.2.6.2 (for a smooth map of relative dimension d with connected geometric fibres, f^*[d] is fully faithful on perverse sheaves and the adjoints pH^d f_!, pH^{-d} f_* identify the largest subobject and quotient from the base) and SS5.4.11-5.4.13 (universal hyperplane family: the maximal-perverse-subobject statement (5.4.11.iii) and the projective-bundle formula (5.4.12)), with de Cataldo-Migliorini Propositions 4.7.8-4.7.9 as an independently printed version. Step 1 (relative weak Lefschetz). Let j be the open inclusion of the complement of the universal incidence and u=(f x 1)j. Over an affine chart of the hyperplane parameter space the complement is an affine d-space bundle, so u is affine. Apply R(f x 1)_! to the localization triangle j_!j^*p'^*K[d] -> p'^*K[d] -> i_*i^*p'^*K[d]. The affine one-sided exactness supplier makes the first term have no negative perverse cohomology; proper base change and the noncharacteristic pullback supplier identify the second with p^*Rf_*K[d] and the third with Rg_*M[1]. The long exact perverse sequence gives the restriction isomorphisms for l<=-2 and the monomorphism for l=-1, and duality gives the Gysin isomorphisms for l>=2 and epimorphism for l=1, with i^!=i^*[-2] in the compatible normalization. Step 2 (projective-bundle formula). Cup powers of the tautological Euler class pulled back from the dual projective space define a morphism from the direct sum; on every fibre it is the standard projective-space cohomology basis, so proper base change proves Rp_*p^*T = sum_{a=0}^{d} T[-2a] for every constructible T, and the same formula with d-1 holds for p'i. The integral power basis is [[lem-complex-tautological-euler-class-restricts-to-the-projective-fiber-generator]] (sphere-bundle Gysin sequence) and finiteness is preserved by [[thm-cellular-cochains-compute-cohomology-with-local-coefficients]]. Consequently Hom(p^*A[d],p^*B[d])=Hom(A,B) for heart objects A,B, since the terms Hom(A,B[-2a]) for a>0 vanish in the heart. Step 3 (maximal subobject and quotient). p^*[d] sends a simple intersection complex to a simple intersection complex and is exact and fully faithful; its image is closed under subobjects and quotients by induction on the finite length of the heart objects, so the perverse adjoints l=pH^d Rp_! and r=pH^{-d} Rp_* identify p^*[d]r(C)->C as the largest subobject and C->p^*[d]l(C) as the largest quotient from Y. Step 4 (truncation). Put V=R(f x 1)_*p'^*K and U=Rg_*i^*p'^*K. Step 1 gives pH tau_{<d-1} V = pH tau_{<d-1} U and a monomorphism pH^{d-1}V -> pH^{d-1}U. The discarded summand Rf_*K[-2d] has perverse amplitude at least d, because every fibre of f has dimension at most d (BBD 4.2.4 amplitude estimates together with the proper adjunctions), so Rp_* of the two truncated triangles shows r(pH^{d-1}V)=r(pH^{d-1}U); since pH^{d-1}V=p^*pH^{-1}(Rf_*K)[d] lies in the pullback image, where r is inverse to p^*[d], naturality identifies its injection into pH^{d-1}U=pH^0(Rg_*M) with the maximal-subobject counit. Dualizing the proved statement for DK gives the maximal-quotient identification p^*pH^1(Rf_*K)[d]. No pure-sheaf, arithmetic-comparison or decomposition-theorem input is used; the affine one-sided exactness and noncharacteristic pullback items are separate necessary suppliers on this page and are not silently identified with the absolute Artin bound.

title: Affine Perverse Vanishing And Universal Hyperplanes Examples

items.title: Universal hyperplanes lower the defect for projective space to a point
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. For $f:\mathbb P^n\to\mathrm{pt}$ with $n\ge1$, the defect is $r(f)=n$. The universal hyperplane family maps to the dual space $(\mathbb P^n)^\vee$ with fibers $\mathbb P^{n-1}$ and has defect $n-1$.
items.strategy: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the cited geometry suppliers. Step 1. For f:P^n->pt with n>=1 the source dimension is n, the only fibre has dimension n, and the image has dimension zero, so the defect r(f)=2n-n=n. The universal incidence is a projective-space bundle over the dual projective space with fibre P^{n-1}, so its total space has dimension 2n-1. Step 2. The only fibre dimension of the universal family is n-1, so its defect is 2(n-1)+n-(2n-1)=n-1, strictly below n; this checks the positive-defect clause of [[lem-projective-hyperplane-sections-decrease-the-defect-of-semismallness]] directly, including n=1, where the universal family is the identity on the dual projective line.
